room.title: IT Admins and Workspace Owners
room.description: How an IT admin rolls a new workspace out department by department and keeps licences and leavers tidy — the wave plan, access groups and policy, the quarterly access review and the offboarding gaps, in one place the service desk works from too.

desks.title: New workspace rollout — waves, groups and access by department
desks.description: Rolling a new collaboration workspace out to 262 staff in three waves: directory groups per department, champions, guest rules and activation by team, with the service desk working from the same plan.
desks.brief:
## New workspace rollout — waves, groups and access

**Organisation** Ridgeway · 262 staff across 10 departments, plus contract drafters
**Sign-in** through the SSO provider with multi-factor authentication, membership synced from directory groups
**Wave 3** starts @+14d

### Plan
- **Wave 1** — IT, Operations, Finance, HR & People. Live since @-19d, 52 of 57 activated
- **Wave 2** — Structural, Civil, Project management office. Started @-5d, 70 of 143 activated
- **Wave 3** — Drafting & BIM, Business development, Leadership. Scheduled; Drafting is blocked on a group clean-up

### Access model
Membership comes from directory groups, never from manual invites. Each department has a champion who answers 'how do I' questions before they become tickets. Contractors and clients come in as guests with a staff sponsor and an expiry date.

### Who works from this desk
Mateo on the service desk and the ten department champions. When someone asks 'is my team live yet?', the answer is a row here rather than a ticket.

### Where it stands
122 of 262 staff activated. Civil engineering is the slowest to activate, and Drafting & BIM can't start until its directory group is split.

callout.title: Blocked: Drafting & BIM group
callout.body: The directory group for Drafting & BIM mixes 34 staff with 11 contract drafters, and contractors must come in as guests, not members. Ngozi is splitting the group. Wave 3 starts @+14d either way; if the split isn't done, Drafting moves to a wave 3b.

children.label: Reviewed in the quarterly access review

blocks.p: Agreed with the department heads @-24d. Applies from wave 1; reviewed once wave 3 is live.

ul: Access comes from the department's directory group — no manual invites
Moving department moves access automatically at the next sync
Leavers lose access when their directory account is disabled
Every guest has a named staff sponsor
Guest access expires after 90 days unless the sponsor renews it
Guests are invited to specific spaces, never the whole workspace
Guests sign in with multi-factor authentication too — no exceptions for clients

blocks.p: Two owners and three admins, all in IT. Admin rights are checked every quarter in the access review — the other desk in this room.

notes.title: Service desk — wave 2 so far
notes.body:
Top tickets since wave 2 started (from Mateo):

- 14 × 'I can't see my project space' — group sync takes up to 40 minutes; now in the welcome email
- 6 × 'can I invite the client?' — guest policy; champions to answer first
- 3 × duplicate accounts from personal sign-ups before the rollout — merge by hand

Civil is slowest (22 of 58). Arjun thinks site staff never saw the email — try five minutes in the site toolbox talks.

desks.title: Quarterly access review — licences, admins and leavers
desks.description: Twelve apps checked against the directory: paid seats against active users, who holds admin rights, and leavers who still have access, with the idle spend this review should recover.
desks.brief:
## Quarterly access review — licences, admins and leavers

**Scope** 12 apps · 262 staff · 14 leavers this quarter
**Sources** directory export, each app's user list, finance's licence register
**Sign-off** app owners by @+5d · summary to the operations director @+7d

### What the review checks
1. **Seats** — paid seats against people active in the last 30 days
2. **Admins** — every admin account has a written reason to exist
3. **Leavers** — nobody who has left still has a working account

### What we found
- **$4,189 a month** in idle seats across the 12 apps; $4,011 of it is recoverable this quarter (about $48k a year)
- **7 leaver accounts** still active — every one in an app outside the SSO provider
- **31 admin accounts**; 9 have no current reason and are being removed

### How sign-off works
Each app owner confirms their row's action on this desk instead of replying to a spreadsheet passed around by email. Finance sees the recoverable spend as each row is agreed, not at quarter end.

callout.title: 7 leaver accounts — all outside SSO
callout.body: Every leaver account still active is in an app that isn't behind the SSO provider: CRM, CAD suite, design tool, survey tool and file transfer. Disable all seven @today, then move the CRM and file transfer behind SSO before next quarter's review.

children.label: Local logins in CRM and CAD
API tokens owned by a person

blocks.p: Runs from the HR leaver ticket. v3 adds the apps outside SSO, because this review found every remaining leaver account there.

ol: Disable the directory account — this ends access to every app behind the SSO provider
Wipe or recover devices through the MDM
Remove mail forwarding and calendar delegates
Rotate any shared account password they knew

blocks.h4: Apps outside SSO — by hand until migrated

ul: Transfer file ownership to their manager
Reclaim the licence seat rather than leaving it idle

notes.title: Admin rights — what I'm cutting
notes.body:
31 admin accounts across the 12 apps. Removing 9:

- 4 in the CRM, left over from a sales ops project that ended
- 2 in the CAD suite, held by people who moved into project roles
- 2 in the chat tool, granted 'temporarily' for last year's migration
- 1 in the survey tool, held by a leaver (also counted in the 7)

Keeping 22, each with its reason written in the licence register.

notes.title: Renewals inside the window
notes.body:
- CAD suite renews @+40d — reclaim the 7 idle seats before then or pay $17,640 for them over another year
- Diagram tool is month to month — cancel now
- Survey tool: 2 active users. Check whether the office suite's forms cover them before cancelling

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
Disable the 7 leaver accounts.
Chase 3 app owners for sign-off.

stickies.title: Next quarter
stickies.body: CRM and file transfer behind SSO.
